title: Convergence rates for sums-of-squares hierarchies with correlative sparsity
authors: Korda, Milan and Magron, Victor and Ríos-Zertuche, Rodolfo
relevance: Nearest primary sparse-hierarchy precedent. Theorem 6 (journal p.444) is sparse Schmüdgen/full-preordering on cube bags under running intersection: p=sum p_j, p>=epsilon on the cube, with coordinatewise degree thresholds r_{j,i}=O(epsilon^{-(w+3)/2}) for fixed instance data; this implies objective gap O(R^{-2/(w+3)}), not a generic O(R^-2). Theorem 8 (pp.445–446) separately treats sparse Putinar/quadratic modules with scaled local generators, local Archimedean certificates, and error-bound exponents. Distinguish the two cones and rate conversions.

title: Squared polynomial approximation kernels for the hypercube: improved error bounds and implications for Lasserre hierarchies
authors: Gribling, Sander and de Klerk, Etienne and Vera, Juan C.
relevance: Primary dense-kernel comparator. Theorem 7 (PDF p.14) bounds the dense ordinary quadratic-module lower-bound gap on [-1,1]^n by c1 n^3 d^2 ||f||_{1,Cheb} log_2^3(r)/r^2 for n dividing r and r/log_2(r)>=c2 n^2 d^2; its hierarchy index is 2r. The module has only the unit SOS term and one (1-x_i^2) localizer at a time, with no products and no correlative sparsity, so it does not imply a sparse-preordering or sparse-module rate.

title: Extension on the convergence rates of moment-SOS hierarchies via approximation of truncated moment sequences
authors: Tran, Hoang Anh and Toh, Kim-Chuan
relevance: Cutoff-sensitive primary follow-up. Theorem 3.1 (PDF p.14) restates the dense ordinary-module O(log^3(r)/r^2) hypercube bound; the paper extends truncated-pseudo-moment estimates to dense Putinar and other hierarchy types. Its conclusion (PDF p.27) explicitly identifies adaptation to sparse descriptions as future work, so it does not establish separator consistency or defeat the sparse-versus-dense distinction.

title: On the convergence rates of moment-SOS hierarchies approximation of truncated moment sequences
authors: Tran, Hoang Anh and Toh, Kim-Chuan
relevance: Related primary predecessor for the truncated-pseudo-moment method, but dense. Theorem 3.5 (arXiv PDF pp.16–17) bounds Hausdorff distance from truncated pseudo-moment sets to true moment sets over products of unit balls/simplexes, and Corollary 3.4 (p.15) gives O(r^-2) for a dense Schmüdgen hierarchy on such products. The factor domains are disjoint product coordinates; the results do not enforce separator consistency across overlapping sparse bags.
